question.problem: Find the $31$st term of an arithmetic sequence given that the $22$nd term is $76$ and the $6$th term is $-4.$
question.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term is given by 

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d,
$$

so we need to figure out the first term ${a}_{1}$ and the common difference $d.$

To find the common difference, we can find the total difference between the terms ${a}_{22}=76$ and ${a}_{6}=-4$ and divide it by the number of jumps, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =\frac{{a}_{22}-{a}_{6}}{22-6} \\  & =\frac{76-(-4)}{22-6} \\  & =\frac{80}{16} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use one of our known values, say, ${a}_{6}=-4,$ to determine the first term of the sequence. Since ${a}_{6}$ is $5$ jumps after ${a}_{1},$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{6} & ={a}_{1}+5d \\ -4 & ={a}_{1}+5\cdot 5 \\ -4 & ={a}_{1}+25 \\ {a}_{1} & =-29\end{aligned}
$$

So the formula for the $n$th term is:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =-29+(n-1)\cdot 5 \\  & =-34+5n\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can find the $31$st term by substituting $n=31$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{31} & =-34+5(31) \\  & =-34+155 \\  & =121\end{aligned}
$$
